verdict.reasoning: Patient mentions severe headaches mainly frontal, palpitations (“my heart is beating kind of fast”), intermittent shortness of breath while sitting, tingling in both hands, reduced appetite, ~5 lb unintentional weight loss, and loss of libido (“some loss of libido at home”).

Patient states symptoms started when he changed jobs (“it’s started roughly when I changed jobs”) and occur at work including in meetings and on laptop (“I’m at work. I’m in a meeting or in my laptop”) and sometimes in the elevator (“especially…when I come into the elevator in the morning”).

Headache location: “No, it’s mostly in the front, and then, yeah, it kind of stays there” (non‑radiating). Occurs during work (“generally during work times”). Associated with mild nausea (“I kind of feel a little bit nauseous, maybe”).
Patient reports with headaches “sometimes I also feel like. Yeah, it’s like maybe probably breathing or something,” indicating a perceived breathing issue accompanying headaches.
On palpitations: “Again, how often do you get that?” / “I like, it’s maybe once a day, maybe more.”
Shortness of breath: “Yes. So do you feel short of breath while you’re sitting at your desk? … ‘Yeah. No. Yes. Sorry. Yeah.’” and “And how about when you’re exercising? ‘No.’”
Tingling: “So talk to me about that. Is it in one hand or both hands? ‘Both.’ … ‘And do you get that in your legs as well? ‘No.’ … ‘What does it feel like? The tingling?’ ‘Prickling? Yeah.’”
Stress: “If 10 out of 10 is extremely stressful…?” / “I think it’s seven or eight.” Job: “I’m a lawyer… Go to meetings and then sit in front of a computer… There’s a lot of reading.”
Past medical history: “Well, I have a hypothyroidism.”
Medication: “And do you take medications for that? ‘Thyroxine.’ … ‘And are you Remembering to take your medications?’ ‘Yes.’”
Allergies: “And are you allergic to anything? ‘No.’” This supports no known drug allergies.
Social history: “So talk to me about your job. What do you do? ‘I’m a lawyer.’… ‘And do you work in London at the moment?’ ‘Yes.’”
Alcohol: “How much do you drink? ‘Like once a week. A couple of glasses.’”
Smoking: “And how about smoking? ‘No.’”
Recreational drugs: “do you do anything else recreational in terms of drugs? ‘No.’ … ‘So you’ve never taken cocaine or marijuana?’ ‘No.’”

Episodic work‑related frontal headaches with mild nausea: derived from “generally during work times,” “mostly in the front,” “it kind of stays there,” and “I kind of feel a little bit nauseous, maybe.” No prior headache history: “And do you normally get headaches before all of this started? ‘So, no…’”

Palpitations and shortness of breath at rest: “I kind of have. My heart is beating kind of fast” and shortness of breath at desk but not with exercise. Temporal link to stress/job change is supported by symptoms beginning when he changed jobs and stress rated 7–8/10 with law‑firm pressure.
Hand paresthesias: “Is it in one hand or both hands? ‘Both.’ … ‘What does it feel like? The tingling?’ ‘Prickling? Yeah.’”

Decreased appetite: “I kind of lose my appetite also.” Weight loss: “Have you lost weight? ‘Yes.’ … ‘5Lbs.’ … ‘It’s not intentional.’” Decreased libido since job change: “There’s one more thing… some loss of libido at home.” / “How long has that been happening for? ‘Same amount of time. Really? Like, since I changed my job.’”
History: “Well, I have a hypothyroidism.” / “Thyroxine.” Plan: “probably do some blood tests for your thyroxin.” This implies thyroid labs to assess replacement status.

Labs: “and probably do some blood tests for your thyroxin.”
